aggressive_definition: PSA-detected high-grade prostate cancer; the abstract does not provide a Gleason threshold for high grade.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: We found evidence of lower PSA (RGM 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.99) and decreased risk of low Gleason-grade (RRR 0.96; 95%CI 0.93-0.99) but increased risk of high-grade prostate cancer (RRR 1.04; 95%CI 0.99-1.08; p(difference) =0.004) per 10 units/week increase in alcohol consumption, not explained by current BMI, blood pressure, comorbidities, or reverse causation.
study_design: Case-control study nested in the PSA-testing phase of the ProtecT randomized trial.
reason: The study evaluated PSA-detected prostate cancer overall and by grade, including an explicitly high-grade incident endpoint. The abstract does not report the number of high-grade cases or a single total analytic sample size.

estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text table evidence explicitly labels this continuous alcohol estimate as total prostate cancer; the abstract does not report this total-disease numeric estimate.
